name: D-Day
hook: June 6, 1944: the beaches, the commanders and the plan behind the largest amphibious invasion ever.

facts.label: June 6, 1944
facts.statement: D-Day was June 6, 1944, when the Allies invaded Normandy in the largest sea and airborne invasion in history.

facts.label: Normandy
facts.statement: The invasion hit the Normandy coast of France, with landing beaches including Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno and Sword.

facts.label: Operation Overlord
facts.statement: The invasion's code name was Operation Overlord, and Dwight D. Eisenhower directed it as supreme Allied commander.

facts.label: Bernard Montgomery
facts.statement: British field marshal Bernard Montgomery commanded all Allied ground forces on D-Day under Eisenhower.

facts.label: COSSAC and the Sussex scheme
facts.statement: The COSSAC plan laid out the invasion, and the 1944 Sussex scheme dropped agents into France ahead of the assault.

facts.label: Saving Private Ryan
facts.statement: Saving Private Ryan opens with the storming of Omaha Beach, recreating the Normandy landings in its first 20 minutes.
